day3_morning_wake_2.text: *My body feels heavy. The hand that silenced the alarm drops onto the blanket a beat late.*

day3_morning_wake_3.text: *I stood in front of the sink to wash my face. The mirror is fogged up. I reached out to wipe it... and stopped.*

day3_morning_mirror_1.text: *The steam runs down, and only the part at eye level clears first. Before I can look at it, I turn on the faucet.*

day3_morning_mirror_2.text: *I only splashed water on my face and left.*

day3_morning_mirror_3.text: *I opened the fridge and... the milk I bought yesterday has been moved.*

day3_morning_milk_1.text: *Only a round water ring remains where it used to be.*

day3_morning_milk_2.text: *The pencil case is on the right. The milk is on the top shelf. Both have been moved somewhere easy for my hand to reach.*

day3_morning_commute_1.text: *I leave the house and head to school. The morning air is cold.*

day3_morning_commute_2.text: *As I walk through an alley, I spot two students ahead. One of them says:*

day3_morning_commute_3.text: Hey, did you do the math homework? Number 2 was kind of hard.

day3_morning_commute_4.text: I looked at the answer key.

day3_morning_commute_5.text: *The next words come to mind first.*

day3_morning_commute_6.text: *The same alley. The same time. The laughter from the person ahead follows half a beat after the sound that played in my head first.*

day3_morning_commute_7.text: *The math printouts hanging from the two students' bags are folded at the same corner as yesterday.*

day3_morning_commute_8.text: *My steps quicken until the strap of my bag bounces against my shoulder.*

day3_morning_gate_1.text: *I arrive at school. Sea is nowhere in sight today.*

day3_morning_gate_2.text: *Beside the brick pillar, the spot where Sea had been leaning is empty. Only the cherry blossom petals on the ground are pressed into the shape of shoes.*

day3_morning_gate_3.text: *I pass through the school gate between the other students. A short voice behind me makes me turn around.*

day3_morning_gate_4.text: *No one looks. Everyone keeps walking straight ahead.*

day3_morning_gate_5.text: *The boy who just passed meets my eyes. His lips move very slightly. No sound. It is close to 'again.'*

day3_morning_gate_6.text: *I turned to look again. He'd already gone inside the building.*

day3_morning_locker_2.text: *A locker. The name has been scratched off. Marks of being scraped repeatedly with a key or knife.*

day3_morning_locker_3.text: *Curious, I open the unlocked locker. It is completely empty except for dust.*

day3_morning_locker_4.text: *In the corner, a torn photo. A passport-sized photo cut in half. Only half a face remains.*

day3_morning_locker_5.text: *This face looks familiar. Who is it?*

day3_morning_photo_1.text: *I put the photo in my pocket.*

day3_morning_photo_2.text: *...And there's one more scratched inscription on the inside wall of the locker. Very small.*

day3_morning_inscription_1.text: *The stroke bending left. The period losing strength at the end. It is the same as what I saw under the desk yesterday.*

day3_morning_inscription_2.text: *I look under my fingernails. The graphite marks from yesterday have already been washed away.*

day3_morning_inscription_3.text: *I close the locker and turn the corner. Seolhwa is standing there. Close this time.*

day3_morning_seolhwa_4.text: ...Huh? Yeah, I am. How did you know?

day3_morning_seolhwa_5.text: *Seolhwa doesn’t answer. She looks once at my left hand and once at my face. After a moment, she speaks quietly.*
choices: Answer the question about my left hand
Ask why she wants to know

day3_morning_seolhwa_8.text:
*Seolhwa turns and walks away.*

Wait. Careful of what? You can't just say that and leave.

day3_morning_seolhwa_9.text: *The fingers of my left hand curl and uncurl on their own. The hand I held out when we greeted each other yesterday was my right.*

day3_morning_classroom_1.text: *I walked down the hallway and stood in front of the classroom. I can hear murmuring beyond the door.*

day3_morning_classroom_4.text: *Chalk dust falls slowly below the blackboard. The laughter does not return.*

day3_morning_classroom_5.text: *Two boys in the front row glance at each other. A girl in the back row turns her gaze out of the window. Under a desk, someone stops a chair leg with the tips of their toes.*

day3_morning_goosebumps.text: *I rub my forearm. The hairs are standing on end. The ticking second hand is the only sound that catches in my ears.*

day3_morning_sea_1a.text: *Sea is sitting at her desk. She's smiling, but only the corners of her mouth have moved.*

day3_morning_sea_2.text: Morning, {name}. You're a bit late today?

day3_morning_sea_4.text: You don't look well. Couldn't sleep last night?

day3_morning_sea_5.text:
*Sea's voice is bright. Her fingers tap a steady rhythm on the desk, pausing twice.*

What were you all talking about? It went quiet when I came in.

day3_morning_sea_6.text:
*Sea's gaze moves down from my face to the nape of my neck, then my left hand, before coming back up.*

I didn't notice you come in. Did you sleep badly last night?

day3_morning_sea_6b.text: *In the margin of Sea's notebook, beside today's date, three small empty squares have been drawn.*

day3_morning_sea_7.text: Yeah, I tossed and turned a bit.

day3_morning_sea_6a.text:
*Sea tilts her head slightly and watches me. 2 seconds. 3. 4.*

Why are you staring? Something on my face?

day3_morning_sea_9.text:
*Sea turns away. The muscles at the back of her neck are taut. A check appears in one of the empty squares she just drew.*

What are you writing? Are you noting down that I slept badly too?

day3_morning_pencil_1.text: *I sit down and open the desk drawer... the pencil case I left yesterday has been moved.*

day3_morning_pencil_2.text: *I definitely put it on the left, but it's on the right.*

day3_morning_end.text: *Class begins. I read the first line of the textbook three times, but my eyes keep returning to the same spot.*

day3_morning_photo_back.text: *I turned the photo fragment over and examined the back. A faint date was written on it.*

day3_morning_photo_look.text: *I kept the photo fragment covered with my hand and turned to look down the corridor.*

day3_morning_photo_back_detail_1.text: When I turned the paper over, I got pencil dust on my fingers. A short note was written on the back of the photo.

day3_morning_photo_back_detail_2.text: #11 — Discard. The underline of the number jumps up from the end. The same spot popped up when I wrote the date in my notebook.

day3_morning_photo_back_detail_3.text: I took out my notebook and placed a photo next to the timetable I wrote down yesterday. Even the angle at which number 1's head was bent was similar.

day3_morning_photo_back_detail_4.text: If I had written it, when would it have been? While I was searching for memories, I heard the hallway window closing.

day3_morning_photo_back_detail_5.text: I traced the spot drawn with the tip of the pencil with my fingernail. The paper was thin, so the strokes were pressed all the way to the front.

day3_morning_photo_back_detail_6.text: I chose a way to check my pencil notes.
choices: Just take a picture and let go.

day3_morning_photo_back_detail_7.text: I took a picture of the memo with my cell phone and inserted the original into my notebook. This time, I used a ruler to keep the edges from folding.

day3_morning_photo_back_detail_8.text: When I looked up, I saw the red light of a camera at the end of the hallway. A small dot moved under the lens.

day3_morning_photo_back_detail_9.text: When I half-closed the locker door, my door was reflected in a black semicircle.

day3_morning_photo_look_detail_1.text: When I held the photo up to the window light, glue from another paper remained between the white fibers at the cut edge.

day3_morning_photo_look_detail_2.text: It was a photo that someone had removed from an album. Only the middle of the back was particularly smooth.

day3_morning_photo_look_detail_3.text: The classroom bulletin board was visible next to the spot where the face was cut off. The current classroom schedule and number of columns were the same.

day3_morning_photo_look_detail_4.text: When I displayed the photo of yesterday's classroom on my phone, even the brown stains on the corners of the bulletin board overlapped.

day3_morning_photo_look_detail_5.text: There was no date on which the photo was taken. The clock was also obscured by the area where the person was standing.

day3_morning_photo_look_detail_6.text: I changed hands before the corners of the photo got wet.
choices: I see it again from the window
Put it in your pocket and go to class.

day3_morning_photo_look_detail_7.text: A short mechanical sound came from the end of the hallway. The camera lens is tilted down ever so slightly.

day3_morning_photo_look_detail_8.text: Movement stopped right above my locker. The red light around the lens stayed on.

day3_morning_photo_look_detail_9.text: I put the photo in my inner pocket and closed the door. The key got stuck and I had to turn it one more time.

day3_morning_class_silence_1.text: When I pushed the door, the sounds of conversation in the classroom stopped and the hands that were turning the pages stopped for a moment.

day3_morning_class_silence_2.text: About twenty kids were looking at the teacher's table. No one turned their head towards the door I came through.

day3_morning_class_silence_3.text: I could hear another class laughing in the hallway. Only the fan near the window in our class was running low.

day3_morning_class_silence_4.text: As I closed the door, one of the chair legs scraped the floor. Only then did Sea smile at me.

day3_morning_class_silence_5.text: There you are. I got your books out for you.

day3_morning_class_silence_6.text: There was a pencil case on the right end of the desk. It was definitely my hand that I put in the front compartment of my bag in the morning.

day3_morning_class_silence_7.text: The boy sitting next to me folded and unfolded the same corner of the textbook and then folded it again.

day3_morning_class_silence_8.text: I put my bag down on the empty chair. Even if I let go of the handle, no conversation continued in the classroom.

day3_morning_class_silence_choice.text: I put my hand between the pencil case and my bag.
choices: Ask the student next to you what he just said
I pretend not to know and open my textbook

day3_morning_class_ask_1.text: The male student looked at my nametag instead of my face. I hid the folded corner of the textbook under my fingers.

day3_morning_class_ask_2.text: I didn't say anything. I was preparing for class.

day3_morning_class_ask_3.text: I asked who came first. The male student turned a page in his textbook and then turned it back.

day3_morning_class_ask_4.text: I didn't say anything. I was preparing for class.

day3_morning_class_ask_5.text: This time, when I called his name, the boy's gaze briefly rose from my name tag to my lips.

day3_morning_class_ask_6.text: You can say your name when they take attendance.

day3_morning_class_ask_7.text: Sea knocked on the desk once. The boy picked up his pencil according to the sound.

day3_morning_class_ask_8.text: He's always quiet in the morning. Open your book. They're checking them today.

day3_morning_class_ask_9.text: I took out a notebook from under the desk and pressed down the page with the photo with my palm instead of unfolding it.

day3_morning_class_sea_1.text: Sea's smile disappeared for a moment. I looked at my hand and my pencil case in turn and raised my eyebrows again.

day3_morning_class_sea_2.text: What? Is there something on my face?

day3_morning_class_sea_3.text: He pointed to the pencil case. Before Sea answered, he moved his pencil case a little to the right.

day3_morning_class_sea_4.text: It was about two fingers away from the edge of the desk. It was placed unusually straight.

day3_morning_class_sea_5.text: Your arm won't catch it here. You nearly knocked it off yesterday too.

day3_morning_class_sea_6.text: I didn't bring my pencil case yesterday. While I was talking, Sea closed the zipper of the bag.

day3_morning_class_sea_7.text: I mean the pen I lent you. Don't you remember?

day3_morning_class_sea_8.text: The pen must have been on the desk. Still, my hand didn't come off the handle of my bag.

day3_morning_class_sea_9.text: Sea first turned his head towards the teaching table. I sat down only after looking at the back of his head.

day3_morning_class_book_1.text: When I opened the textbook, a folded page immediately appeared. It was two chapters ahead of the section I was looking for.

day3_morning_class_book_2.text: While I was pressing the corner of the book to open it, I heard the sound of a pencil coming from the seat next to me. I also wrote the date according to that sound.

day3_morning_class_book_3.text: Wrong page. We're on the next chapter.

day3_morning_class_book_4.text: As I turned the two pages without saying a word, Sea opened his book only after I had turned to the correct page.

day3_morning_class_book_5.text: I heard a small laugh coming from the hallway door, and when I turned around, I saw a student behind me looking at the empty blackboard.

day3_morning_class_book_6.text: I erased the date written at the top of the note and rewrote it. I wrote the same number twice, but it looked different.

day3_morning_class_book_7.text: White powder fell on the chalk base. The sound of the teacher's shoes outside the door got closer.

day3_morning_class_resume_1.text: When the door opened, the children greeted us. The first syllable of the sound was not out of sync.

day3_morning_class_resume_2.text: The teacher opened the attendance sheet and looked between the desks. As he passed my seat, his gaze lowered slightly.

day3_morning_class_resume_3.text: Let's start class. Today, don't erase what you wrote down, just leave it as is.

day3_morning_class_resume_4.text: I put the eraser on the note. The date I had just corrected looked like a different number because the pencil marks overlapped.

day3_history_callback_10.text: I took out the wet paper from the back of the notebook and took a picture of the smudged strokes and the photo note on the same page.

day3_history_callback_11.text: I placed the photo I received on the first day next to it. The height of the bulletin board was the same, but the only difference was the position of the person who took the photo.

day3_history_callback_12.text: I had asked Sea the same question on the first day, but this time I didn't just laugh it off and waited for the answer.

day3_history_callback_13.text: The pen I was holding with my left hand rolled around inside the pencil case. Sea pressed his hand against the pencil case until the sound stopped.

day3_history_callback_14.text: I stopped to look at the paper photo I had left in the drawer. Even if you hide your phone behind a textbook, the light from the screen remains on the back of your hand.

day3_expansion_action_4_a.text: There was no eraser on the original. I dropped my pencil-dusted finger from the photo and covered the notebook.

day3_expansion_action_4_b.text: I tried to trace it the same way, but the end of the underline jumped to the other side. I left the two letters side by side without forcing them to be corrected.

day3_expansion_action_5_a.text: The shadow of the window frame passed over the photo. When the light changed, a pushpin on the bulletin board behind the figure became visible.

day3_expansion_action_5_b.text: I unfolded the pocket lining, inserted the photo, and moved the bag strap to the opposite shoulder to prevent it from folding while walking.
